name: Skeuomorphism
definition: A style that makes interface elements imitate real objects and materials, using leather, metal, paper, and glossy highlights so their purpose reads as familiar.
useWhen: the control is dressed as the physical object it replaces

sources.title: Skeuomorphism | Aesthetics Wiki
NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

notes: The reference pole for the whole category: half the other entries are defined against it.

name: Flat design
definition: A style that strips away depth cues, using solid fills, sharp edges, and bold color instead of shadow, gradient, bevel, or texture.
useWhen: no depth cues at all, only color and shape

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
CareerFoundry: Flat Design: A Complete Beginner's Guide

notes: Datable: emerged around 2011, mainstreamed by Windows Metro and iOS 7.

name: Flat 2.0
definition: Flat design with the depth cues put back in small doses: soft shadow, subtle gradient, and hover feedback that show what can actually be clicked.
useWhen: flat surfaces, but affordance restored with light shadow

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
UXPin: The 7-Minute Guide to Flat Design 2.0

notes: NN/g owns this coinage; 99designs and others say semi-flat for the same thing. Merge candidate with flat-design if the taxonomy prefers one entry with a history section.

name: Minimalism
definition: A style that reduces an interface to one typeface, one accent color, and generous empty space, letting whitespace rather than ornament carry hierarchy.
useWhen: hierarchy carried by space, not by decoration

sources.title: Superdesign: UI style catalog
Zoviz: Minimalist vs Maximalist Web Design

name: Maximalism
definition: A style that fills the screen on purpose with layered color, pattern, and type, treating abundance rather than restraint as the message.
useWhen: abundance is the point, not a failure of editing

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Battle of the Divisive Design Styles
Twine: Minimalism vs Maximalism: The Pros and Cons for Web Design

name: Anti-design
definition: A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.
useWhen: the rule breaking is the message

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Battle of the Divisive Design Styles

notes: Frequently conflated with brutalism; the discrimination is intent (statement) versus method (exposed structure).

name: Brutalist web design
definition: A raw style that leaves the document showing: system or monospace type, default link blue, hard borders, and no decoration beyond structure.
useWhen: the page looks like unstyled HTML on purpose

sources.title: Superdesign: Brutalist Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data
NameThatUI: Neobrutalism

notes: Distinct from neubrutalism: brutalism deletes decoration, neubrutalism adds thick outlines and hard shadows.

name: Neubrutalism
definition: A loud style built from thick black outlines, saturated flat color, square corners, and hard offset shadows with zero blur.
useWhen: black outline plus a hard unblurred shadow

sources.title: NN/g: Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices
NameThatUI: Neobrutalism

notes: Spelling is genuinely split: NN/g writes neobrutalism, the neubrutalism.com guide writes neubrutalism. Both spellings must resolve.

name: Claymorphism
definition: A soft style where controls look inflated from clay: pastel fills, very large corner radii, an inner highlight, and a tinted drop shadow.
useWhen: puffy pastel surfaces that look moulded

sources.title: Superdesign: UI style catalog
Wow-How: 4 Main Types of Morphism in UI Design

name: Aurora UI
definition: A style whose background is built from heavily blurred color blobs that glow and drift like the northern lights behind the content.
useWhen: the background is soft glowing bands of color

sources.title: Hype4 Academy: Aurora UI, new visual trend for 2021
Superdesign: Aurora UI: The CSS Gradient Recipe, Real Examples, and When It Breaks

notes: Coined by Michal Malewicz in 2020/2021. Distinguish from mesh gradient: aurora is the dark, often animated northern-lights case.

name: Mesh gradient
definition: A fill blended from several color points spread across a surface, so the transitions curve and pool instead of running in one straight direction.
useWhen: colors blend from many points, not along one axis

sources.title: DesignerUp: UI Color Gradients: How To Create Mesh, Aurora, and Blended Gradients

notes: Cross-category: recorded as color, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep. SwiftUI shipped a MeshGradient view; worth a verification probe at canonicalize.

name: Grainy gradient
definition: A gradient with a fine noise layer over it, added to hide banding and give a flat background the texture of printed paper or film.
useWhen: a smooth background deliberately roughened with noise

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: Grainy Gradients
ibelick: Creating grainy backgrounds with CSS

notes: Merge candidate: a separate noise-texture entry would overlap almost entirely, so aliases carry it here.

name: Liquid Glass
definition: Apple's 2025 material where controls float as a translucent layer that refracts what is behind them and reshapes fluidly as content moves underneath.
useWhen: controls are a glass layer that bends the content behind

sources.title: Wikipedia: Liquid Glass
WWDC25: Meet Liquid Glass

notes: Announced 9 June 2025 across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, watchOS 26. The HIG page fetch returned only a title (JS rendered), so the URL resolves but its wording was not read this sweep.

name: Acrylic
definition: Fluent's semi-transparent material that blurs, tints, and adds noise to whatever sits behind it, used on transient surfaces like flyouts and menus.
useWhen: a frosted Windows surface you can see the desktop through

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Materials used in Windows apps

notes: Microsoft's recipe is documented explicitly: background, blur, exclusion blend, color tint, noise.

name: Mica
definition: Fluent's opaque app background material, subtly tinted with the user's desktop wallpaper color and going neutral when the window loses focus.
useWhen: an opaque window background tinted by the wallpaper

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Materials used in Windows apps

notes: Shares the wallpaper-personalization idea with Material You, from the opposite vendor. Good contrastWith pair with acrylic (opaque versus transient).

name: Vibrancy
definition: A treatment that samples the color behind a translucent surface and adapts the text and icons drawn on it so they stay legible as the backdrop changes.
useWhen: foreground color adapts to whatever shows through

sources.title: WWDC23: Design for spatial user interfaces
Create with Swift: Ensuring interface legibility and contrast in visionOS

notes: Tail gold: the word most people reach for is just blur, but vibrancy names the legibility half of the effect.

name: Windows Aero
definition: The Windows Vista and 7 look built on translucent glass window frames, soft outer glows, reflections, and animated window transitions.
useWhen: see-through window chrome from the Vista and 7 era

sources.title: NameThatUI: visual style catalog
Wikipedia: Liquid Glass

notes: Named separately from Frutiger Aero: Aero is the Microsoft product design language, Frutiger Aero the wider cultural aesthetic it belongs to.

name: Aqua
definition: Apple's early Mac OS X look of glossy blue gel buttons, pinstripes, gumdrop window controls, and a pulsing default button.
useWhen: candy-gel Mac controls from the 2000s

sources.title: Wikipedia: Aqua (user interface)
NameThatUI: Aqua

notes: Introduced January 2000, shipped in Mac OS X 10.0; flattened out from OS X Yosemite in 2014.

name: Frutiger Aero
definition: The mid 2000s look of glossy gradients, bubbles, water, bright skies, and clean humanist type, retroactively named after the typeface and Windows Aero.
useWhen: glossy optimistic 2000s tech imagery

sources.title: Frutiger Aero | Aesthetics Wiki
Kittl: Frutiger Aero aesthetic

notes: Term coined retroactively by Sofi Lee in 2017, popular from 2022. Covers roughly 2004 to 2013, ended by flat design and iOS 7.

name: Y2K aesthetic
definition: The turn of the millennium look of chrome type, bubble shapes, translucent plastic, and lens flares, revived as a web and app style.
useWhen: chrome, bubbles, and translucent plastic futurism

sources.title: NameThatUI: visual style catalog
Frutiger Aero | 2000 Aesthetics Wiki

name: Vaporwave
definition: A retro internet look of magenta and cyan gradients, grid horizons, Japanese type, statuary, and 90s desktop chrome used ironically.
useWhen: 90s mall and desktop imagery reused with irony

sources.title: Vaporwave | Aesthetics Wiki
Shutterstock: What Is the Vaporwave Aesthetic

name: Synthwave
definition: A neon 1980s look built on sunset gradients, glowing perspective grids, and chrome type, close to vaporwave but sincere rather than ironic.
useWhen: neon grid and sunset 80s futurism, played straight

sources.title: Vaporwave | Aesthetics Wiki
Digital Heroes: Vaporwave Retro Brand Design 2026

notes: Merge candidate with vaporwave if the taxonomy wants one entry; the irony versus sincerity split is the only real discriminator.

name: Retro web design
definition: A style that rebuilds the early desktop web on purpose: beveled window chrome, pixel and system type, garish color, and animated banners.
useWhen: the page imitates a 90s desktop or an early website

sources.title: Superdesign: Retro Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data
Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a 2026 field guide

notes: 98.css recreates Windows 98; system.css recreates Apple System 6 (1984 to 1991).

name: Vernacular web
definition: The amateur homepage look of the GeoCities era: tiled backgrounds, sparkle GIFs, under construction signs, midi music, and hit counters.
useWhen: the hand-made amateur homepage look

sources.title: NameThatUI: visual style catalog

notes: The phrase comes from Olia Lialina's essay A Vernacular Web; that attribution was not verified this sweep and should be checked before publishing.

name: Pixel art UI
definition: An interface drawn on a visible pixel grid, with bitmap type, hard aliased edges, and icons kept at their original low resolution.
useWhen: the pixels are meant to be visible

sources.title: Sage: Retro Web Design: When Pixel Art Belongs on Your Site

notes: The load-bearing CSS is image-rendering: pixelated plus an integer scale factor.

name: Scanlines
definition: Thin repeating dark lines laid over an interface to imitate the raster of a cathode ray tube screen, often with a slight curve and flicker.
useWhen: the screen is dressed as an old CRT monitor

sources.title: Superdesign: Retro Web Design

notes: Classic long-tail query: people search for the word for the lines over a retro screen.

name: Dithering
definition: Simulating shades a palette does not contain by interleaving pixels of the colors it does have, giving images a speckled retro look.
useWhen: shades faked by interleaving a tiny palette

sources.title: TechOps Asia: The Dithering Renaissance: How Retro Graphics Are Shaping Modern Design

notes: Started as a compression constraint, now a deliberate style. Distinguish from halftone (print dots of varying size).

name: Halftone
definition: Rendering tone as a grid of dots that vary in size, borrowed from print and used to give flat interface art a comic or newsprint feel.
useWhen: tone made of print dots that grow and shrink
notes: Frequently confused with dithering; the discrimination is varying dot size versus interleaved fixed pixels.

name: Risograph style
definition: A print-inspired look of two or three flat spot colors that misregister slightly and show grain, imitating a riso duplicator.
useWhen: flat spot colors that overprint and slip out of register
notes: No authoritative UI-side source found this sweep; the term is well established in illustration and increasingly used for web backgrounds. Verify before promoting past stub.

name: Glitch aesthetic
definition: A look that fakes signal failure with color channel offset, torn scan bands, and jitter, used for emphasis or as a whole visual identity.
useWhen: deliberate corruption used as decoration

sources.title: Photoshop Supply: Dither Patterns

notes: Chromatic aberration is listed as an alias rather than its own record; split it out at canonicalize if the demo differs.

name: Memphis design
definition: The 1980s Memphis Group look of clashing pastels, squiggles, confetti dots, and terrazzo shapes scattered across a layout.
useWhen: squiggles and confetti shapes on clashing pastels

sources.title: Wikipedia: Corporate Memphis

notes: Must be disambiguated from Corporate Memphis, which only borrows the name.

name: Corporate Memphis
definition: The flat vector illustration style of bright, faceless people with long bendy limbs and small torsos that spread across tech marketing from 2017.
useWhen: flat faceless people with long bendy limbs

sources.title: Wikipedia: Corporate Memphis
Webflow: Blue people and long limbs: How one illustration style took over the corporate world

notes: Named after the Memphis Group but visually unrelated to it; Alegria (Facebook, 2017) is the origin point.

name: Swiss style
definition: The Swiss modernist system of a strict grid, flush left sans serif type, asymmetric layout, and objective photography, still the base of clean UI layout.
useWhen: grid, Helvetica, and nothing decorative

sources.title: Wikipedia: International Typographic Style
Wikipedia: Swiss Style (design)

notes: Ancestor of the 12-column grid and of most design system layout thinking.

name: Metro
definition: Microsoft's typography led design language of flat colored tiles, large light headings, and motion used in place of chrome, shadow, and texture.
useWhen: flat colored tiles and oversized light headings
notes: Historically important as the trigger for flat design, but no authoritative live source captured this sweep. Verify against Microsoft or Wikipedia before authoring.

name: Material You
definition: Google's personalization layer where the system derives an app's entire color scheme from the user's wallpaper, so every app shifts together.
useWhen: the palette comes from the user's wallpaper

sources.title: Android Developers: Dynamic color

notes: Overlaps the color category; recorded as aesthetic because Material You names a whole design language, not just a palette. Variants documented: Tonal Spot (Android 12), Neutral, Vibrant, Expressive (Android 13).

name: Material 3 Expressive
definition: Google's 2025 update to Material 3, with bolder shapes, larger type, spring based motion physics, and a wider set of dynamic color variants.
useWhen: Material turned up: big shapes, springy motion

sources.title: Google blog: Material 3 Expressive redesign for Android and Wear OS

notes: Announced May 2025, shipped on Pixel with Android 16 in September 2025.

name: Neo-skeuomorphism
definition: The current return of depth and material to interfaces, using restrained texture, shadow, and highlight instead of literal leather, metal, and felt.
useWhen: depth is back, but abstracted rather than literal

sources.title: Userology: Flat Design is Dead: The Rise of Neo-Skeuomorphism in 2026
Versions: The Evolution of Skeuomorphism

notes: Trend-piece vocabulary rather than a settled term; keep as a stub unless the usage holds.

name: Spatial UI
definition: Interface designed to sit in three dimensional space, where panels use a system glass material and depth rather than color carries hierarchy.
useWhen: the interface floats in the room, not on a screen

sources.title: WWDC23: Design for spatial user interfaces
Create with Swift: Ensuring interface legibility and contrast in visionOS

notes: Marked demo: none because a flat specimen cannot honestly show a spatial subject. Reconsider if a parallax mock is judged fair.

name: Long shadow
definition: A flat era decoration where an icon casts a single hard shadow at 45 degrees that runs far past the shape before fading out.
useWhen: one hard 45 degree shadow running off the icon

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

notes: NN/g cites it as flat 2.0 gone wrong: decorative depth that carries no information.

name: Bevel and emboss
definition: Light and dark edges drawn along a shape's border so it reads as raised or carved, the depth trick behind classic desktop buttons.
useWhen: a raised edge drawn from a light and a dark border

sources.title: 98.css

notes: CSS still ships border-style: outset/inset/ridge/groove for exactly this; a good specimen shows all four.

name: Letterpress text
definition: A text effect that fakes stamping into the surface, using a one pixel light shadow below the glyphs and a slightly darker fill above it.
useWhen: type that looks pressed into the surface
notes: Cross-category candidate with typography; kept here because it is a finish, not a type decision.

name: Gloss
definition: A wet plastic finish made from a light gradient across the top half of a control, a highlight arc, and a darker lower half.
useWhen: the control looks like polished wet plastic

sources.title: GirlieMac: CSS3 Gradients: No Image Aqua Button

name: Specular highlight
definition: The bright reflection drawn on a surface to say it is glossy, placed where a light source would strike a curved object.
useWhen: the bright spot that makes a surface read as shiny

sources.title: Wikipedia: Aqua (user interface)

notes: Deep tail: the word for the small bright arc, distinct from the whole gloss treatment. Apple's Liquid Glass documentation uses the term for its edge reflections.

name: Squircle
definition: A rounded square whose corners curve continuously into the sides instead of meeting a circular arc, the shape behind iOS app icons.
useWhen: corners that blend in rather than snap to an arc
notes: Tail gold and highly searched. CSS corner-shape: squircle was landing in browsers around 2025; verify support and the exact property name before authoring.

name: Organic blob
definition: A soft irregular shape with no straight edges, used as a background accent or image mask to soften a strictly rectangular layout.
useWhen: an amoeba shape softening a rectangular grid
notes: Made in CSS with eight-value border-radius, or with an SVG path.

name: Hand-drawn UI
definition: A style whose lines wobble as if sketched by hand, used to signal that a diagram or wireframe is provisional rather than finished.
useWhen: the sketchiness says this is not final yet

sources.title: Wired Elements
Excalidraw

notes: Rough.js is the underlying renderer for both; add it as a system id at canonicalize.

name: Isometric illustration
definition: Art drawn on a fixed axonometric grid so depth reads without perspective, with parallel edges and no vanishing point.
useWhen: depth without perspective, on a fixed 30 degree grid

name: Duotone
definition: An image mapped to exactly two colors, one carrying the shadows and one the highlights, so photography takes on a brand palette.
useWhen: photos forced into two brand colors
notes: Cross-category: recorded as color but discovered in the aesthetic sweep. Doable inline with SVG feColorMatrix or CSS filter plus blend modes.

name: Scrim
definition: A translucent layer laid over content to dim it while a dialog or sheet is open, signalling that everything beneath is out of reach.
useWhen: the dimmed layer behind a modal surface

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Materials used in Windows apps

notes: Cross-category: filed as component, arguably layout. Strong candidate for merging into modal-dialog if the taxonomy prefers parts over standalone entries; Material calls it scrim, Fluent calls it smoke.

name: Dark mode
definition: A designed dark theme with its own surface tiers, desaturated accents, and off-white text, rather than an inversion of the light palette.
useWhen: a dark theme designed, not inverted

sources.title: Superdesign: UI style catalog

notes: Cross-category: recorded as color. Almost certainly enumerated by the color sweep too; dedupe there.

name: Terminal aesthetic
definition: A look borrowed from the command line: monospace type on a fixed character grid, a block cursor, and green or amber text on black.
useWhen: the UI dressed as a command line

sources.title: Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a 2026 field guide

name: Neon glow
definition: A saturated color surrounded by layered soft shadows of the same hue, so type or a border reads as a lit tube against a dark surface.
useWhen: type or borders that look lit rather than filled
notes: Built from stacked text-shadow or box-shadow at increasing blur radii; bloom is the same idea in rendering vocabulary.

name: Editorial web design
definition: A style that borrows print magazine craft for the screen: a visible column grid, display type at poster scale, pull quotes, rules, and captioned images set into the text.
useWhen: a page styled like a magazine spread rather than a template

sources.title: Speckyboy: Modern magazine web layouts
Wix: The biggest web design trends of 2026

notes: Overlaps the layout record magazine-layout, which owns the grid mechanics; this entry is the visual style. Merge candidate at canonicalize.

name: Fictional user interface
definition: The screen graphics style invented for film, television, and games: dense readouts, targeting reticles, wireframe globes, and animated telemetry that look computational without computing anything.
useWhen: interface art made to be watched rather than used

sources.title: Reel Deal Film School: Creating Fantasy User Interfaces (FUIs)
Kit FUI: user interfaces from movies, TV and video games

notes: The F is expanded as fictional, fantasy, futuristic, film, or fake depending on who is writing; fictional is the least contested. HUD is the in-world subset.

name: Terrazzo
definition: A background pattern of small irregular chips scattered on a plain field, copied from poured stone flooring and used flat and multicolored behind interface content.
useWhen: a speckled chip pattern used as a background fill

sources.title: Creative Market: Design Trend Report: Terrazzo
Desenio: Design focus, terrazzo

notes: Named in the memphis-design definition already; kept separate because it is used on its own as a pattern fill with no other Memphis cues.

name: Low poly
definition: A 3D style that keeps the polygon count low enough to see, so surfaces read as faceted triangles under flat shading instead of smooth curves.
useWhen: deliberately faceted 3D art with visible triangles

sources.title: Aesthetics of Design: Low Poly Aesthetic
Sessions College: What is the deal with low poly art?

notes: Started as a rendering budget in games and became a look; flat shading, not the triangle count alone, is what makes it read as a style.

name: Gradient border
definition: An outline filled with a gradient rather than a single color, usually built from a conic or linear gradient behind a masked shape so the hue travels around the edge.
useWhen: an outline whose color changes along its length

sources.title: web.dev: Use conic gradients to create a cool border
Bram.us: Animating a CSS Gradient Border
Bejamas: Finding the best way to create animated gradient borders in CSS

notes: border-image with a gradient works but cannot be animated directly; the rotating version needs a registered @property angle or a pseudo-element.

name: Retro-futurism
definition: A style that pictures the future the way an earlier decade pictured it, so the technology on screen is advanced but the type, color, and hardware belong to the past.
useWhen: a future imagined by an older decade, not by this one

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Retrofuturism
Wikipedia: Raygun Gothic

notes: Umbrella term; its dated subgenres (raygun gothic, atompunk, space age, cassette futurism, Y2K futurism) are separate names, not synonyms.

name: Cassette futurism
definition: The analog future of late 1970s science fiction: beige and putty plastic, chunky toggles and rocker switches, amber or green CRT readouts, and monochrome bitmap type.
useWhen: a future built from 1970s and 80s analog hardware

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Cassette Futurism
TV Tropes: Cassette Futurism

notes: Distinguished from synthwave and vaporwave by materiality: worn utilitarian hardware rather than neon and gradients.

name: Cyberpunk UI
definition: A dystopian sci-fi interface style: near-black surfaces, one or two toxic neon accents, monospace all-caps labels, clipped corners, and scanline or glitch noise laid over the top.
useWhen: dark dystopian surfaces with toxic neon accents

sources.title: stellae.design: Cyberpunk UI, dark themes, neon accents and terminal aesthetics
daisyUI trends: Cyberpunk UI design style

notes: Reads as a bundle: it is mostly dark-mode plus neon-glow plus terminal-aesthetic plus scanlines, so canonicalize may prefer it as a collection page.

name: E-ink aesthetic
definition: A paper-like style built for or borrowed from electronic ink: near-white ground, pure black text, hairline rules, no shadows or gradients, and paged navigation instead of smooth scrolling.
useWhen: an interface styled like reflective ink on paper

sources.title: Intent: How to design for e-ink devices
CHI 2026: A Dedicated E-Paper Design System for Mobile Phones

notes: On real e-paper the constraints are physical (slow refresh, ghosting, no backlight); as a style on ordinary screens it keeps only the look.

name: Biophilic design
definition: A style that borrows from the natural world on purpose, using earthy greens and clays, organic silhouettes, botanical imagery, and slow ambient motion to make a screen feel less mechanical.
useWhen: nature borrowed deliberately for calm, not decoration

sources.title: freeCodeCamp: What is Biophilic Design?
Silphium Design: Understanding biophilia in digital design

notes: Biomimetic is folded in as an alias but is not strictly a synonym: biophilia is about evoking nature, biomimicry about copying how nature works.

name: Deformable UI
definition: A style where controls behave like soft matter, squashing under a press and springing back past rest, so the surface reads as jelly, clay, or inflated plastic rather than paint.
useWhen: controls that squash and spring like soft material

sources.title: UI Style Guide: Tactile Digital / Deformable UI
Buzzvel: The human touch returns, design trends for 2026

notes: Half aesthetic and half motion: the look is claymorphism, the term is really about the spring response on press. Candidate for a motion cross-reference.

name: Retro film aesthetic
definition: A treatment that makes digital imagery look shot on film, adding grain, halation, light leaks, faded contrast, dust, and sometimes a corner date stamp.
useWhen: photography faked to look developed rather than rendered

sources.title: Wix: The biggest web design trends of 2026 (vintage photography and texture)

notes: Overlaps grainy-gradient, which covers noise over a flat fill; this record is the photographic treatment. Merge candidate.

name: VHS aesthetic
definition: A look that imitates a worn videotape: tracking bands, smeared color bleeding past edges, interlace comb artifacts, and burned-in timecode or REC overlays.
useWhen: artifacts of magnetic tape used as decoration

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Retrofuturism (analog subgenres)

notes: Distinct from scanlines (CRT raster) and from glitch (digital failure): the artifacts here are magnetic and horizontal.

name: Hyperreal 3D
definition: Rendered objects pushed past photographic realism, with physically based materials, sharp specular detail, and studio lighting, floated over an otherwise plain interface.
useWhen: a rendered hero object that outdoes a photograph

sources.title: wings.design: 3D and depth in UI, function versus aesthetic

notes: Opposite pole from low-poly on the same axis; usually delivered as a pre-rendered image or a WebGL scene rather than as CSS.

name: Kinetic typography
definition: Type animated over time, where letters and words move, scale, stagger, or morph so the setting carries tone and emphasis that a static line cannot.
useWhen: the type itself performs rather than sits still

sources.title: SVGator: What is kinetic typography, a guide to text in motion
Linearity: Kinetic typography, the what, why and how
Kinetic Typography UX: principles, patterns, and getting started

notes: Cross-category: recorded as typography, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep, and defensible as motion too. Word or letter splitting plus stagger is the usual mechanism, so it also touches the stagger term.

name: Zero UI
definition: A paradigm where the screen stops being the interface and the interaction happens through voice, gesture, presence, or sensors, so the system responds without anything to look at.
useWhen: the interaction has no screen to design

sources.title: Designer Daily: The invisible interface, an introduction to designing for Zero UI
Microsoft Advertising: Zero UI, the invisible interface revolution
UX Planet: Zero UI, how to design invisible interfaces

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep from a style catalog that files it as a look. Nothing to demo on a web page, hence demo none.

name: Generative UI
definition: An interface whose parts are chosen or composed by a model at runtime, so a request is answered with a built form, chart, or panel instead of a paragraph of text.
useWhen: the model assembles the screen, not just the words

sources.title: CopilotKit: Generative UI, understanding agent-powered interfaces
Builder.io: Designing generative UI in an agent-native world
Eleken: Inside generative UI in 2026

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep. Generative UI is the settled engineering name; AI-native UI is the trend-article name for the same thing.

name: Multimodal interface
definition: An interface that accepts and answers in more than one channel at once, letting a person speak, type, touch, or point and pick whichever suits the moment.
useWhen: voice, touch, and screen share one interaction

sources.title: NN/g: Voice First, the future of interaction?
UXmatters: Voice first versus the multimodal user interfaces of the future

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep of a catalog that lists voice-first multimodal as a style. Voice-first is the stricter claim, that voice leads and the screen assists.

name: Art Deco
definition: A 1920s luxury style of strict symmetry, stepped and fanned geometry, strong vertical emphasis, metallic gold on deep color, and high contrast display capitals.
useWhen: symmetrical geometric luxury, gold on deep color

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Big Human: 12 graphic design styles, a complete guide for 2026

notes: Reaches interfaces mainly through display type, borders, and frame ornament rather than through control design.

name: Bauhaus style
definition: A style reduced to primary red, yellow, and blue on off-white, elementary circles, triangles, and squares, and undecorated sans serif type, following form follows function.
useWhen: primary colors and elementary shapes doing the work

sources.title: Digital Heroes: Bauhaus web design, form follows function revival
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Ancestor of swiss-style and of flat-design; the three are often conflated in trend writing, and the primary palette is what separates this one.

name: De Stijl
definition: A style built only from black rules, rectangular fields, and the three primaries on white, arranged asymmetrically with no curves and no diagonals.
useWhen: black rules and primary rectangles, nothing else

sources.title: Creative Market: Design trend report, De Stijl design

notes: Often invoked as the ancestor of card and grid layout; useful on the site as the contrast case for a modular grid.

name: Mid-century modern
definition: A 1950s and 60s style of muted mustard, teal, and burnt orange, tapered organic shapes, textured paper grounds, and friendly geometric sans type.
useWhen: muted 50s palette with tapered organic shapes

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: The optimistic half of the same era that raygun gothic and atompunk draw on, which is why it keeps appearing next to retro-futurism.

name: Kawaii UI
definition: A cute style of pastel fills, rounded everything, oversized eyes and blush marks, sticker and mascot characters, and hand-lettered or bubbly rounded type.
useWhen: cuteness carried by mascots, pastels, and round shapes

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Japanese in origin and still the default register for consumer apps there; mascots do real work, standing in for empty states and errors.

name: Steampunk
definition: A Victorian industrial style of brass, riveted plate, wood, and leather, with gauges, cogs, and valve controls standing in for ordinary interface widgets.
useWhen: brass gauges and cogs instead of plain controls

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
My Steampunk Style: What is retro-futurism?

notes: The clearest surviving case of full skeuomorphism in themes and games; dieselpunk is folded in as an alias but is a later decade.

name: Art Nouveau
definition: A turn of the century style of whiplash curves, botanical line ornament, muted jewel tones, and lettering drawn to fit the frame rather than set on a grid.
useWhen: botanical line ornament and curved frames

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Reaches the screen mostly as ornament and border art; its lettering is the direct ancestor of the psychedelic poster style.

name: Psychedelic style
definition: A 1960s poster style of vibrating complementary color, warped and interlocking lettering that fills its own shape, kaleidoscopic symmetry, and liquid distortion.
useWhen: vibrating color and lettering warped to fill a shape

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Legibility is traded for texture on purpose, which puts it next to anti-design when it is used on a live interface.

name: Grunge design
definition: A 1990s style of torn and photocopied texture, overlapped and cut type, off-grid layout, and dirty muted color, where legibility is traded for emotional pitch.
useWhen: distressed texture and type deliberately off-grid

sources.title: Sessions College: The grunge typography of David Carson
Mew Design Docs: Grunge graphic design, the raw distressed art of the 90s

notes: David Carson at Ray Gun is the reference; the digital revival keeps the texture and the cut type but usually restores a readable body copy.

name: Pop art style
definition: A comic and advertising style of flat primary color, heavy black outlines, printed dot shading, speech balloons, and bold condensed capitals.
useWhen: comic outlines, flat primaries, and printed dots

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Shares its dot shading with halftone and its heavy outlines with neubrutalism, so canonicalize should decide whether it survives as its own entry.

name: Solarpunk
definition: An optimistic ecological future style of daylight palettes, plant growth over structure, stained glass color, art nouveau curves, and visible solar and wind technology.
useWhen: a hopeful green future rather than a dystopian one

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Solarpunk

notes: Defined against cyberpunk on purpose: same technology, opposite politics and palette.

name: Afrofuturism
definition: A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.
useWhen: a future told through African diaspora imagery

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Afrofuturism
Wikipedia: Afrofuturism

notes: Cultural movement first and a visual style second, so a term page has to say that rather than reduce it to pattern and palette.

name: Acid graphics
definition: A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated color on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.
useWhen: chrome, warped type, and rave motifs used ironically

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design: Acid graphics are the new psychedelia
Aesthetics Wiki: Acid Design

notes: Rooted in 1990s acid house flyers rather than 1960s psychedelia, and carries irony where the 60s style carried optimism.

name: Diegetic interface
definition: An interface that exists inside the fiction it serves, so the character can see and use it too, rather than being drawn on top of the world for the player alone.
useWhen: the readout belongs to the world, not the screen

sources.title: TV Tropes: Diegetic Interface
Types of UI in gaming: diegetic, non-diegetic, spatial and meta
Nasty Rodent: Diegetic vs non-diegetic UI, the four-type framework

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep. From the 2009 Fagerholt and Lorentzon thesis, whose four types are fiction against geometry; the other three names are listed as aliases only because they come as a set.

name: Digital collage
definition: A composition assembled from cut-out photography, torn paper edges, scanned texture, and type set at odd angles, so the page reads as pasted up rather than laid out.
useWhen: imagery cut out and pasted rather than placed

sources.title: Linearity: Everything designers need to know about digital collage
Envato: Trend deep dive, collage art

notes: The torn edge and the visible scan texture are what sell it; without them it reads as ordinary image composition.

name: Progressive blur
definition: A blur whose strength ramps across a region instead of applying evenly, so content fades into softness toward an edge rather than stopping at a hard line.
useWhen: content should dissolve into blur, not meet an edge

sources.title: kennethnym: Progressive blur in CSS
Devs Love Coffee: Making Apple progressive blur on the web

notes: Built today by stacking backdrop-filter layers under mask-image gradients; a CSS proposal to give blur() a from and to pair would replace the stack.

name: Holographic foil
definition: A finish that shifts hue with viewing angle, imitating foil, soap film, or a CD surface with banded rainbow gradients over a pale metallic ground.
useWhen: a surface whose color shifts as if it were foil

sources.title: Envato Tuts+: 100+ best holographic and iridescent textures
Effect Labs: CSS holographic effect, iridescent and chrome

notes: The convincing version needs the hue to respond to something, pointer position or scroll, since a static rainbow gradient reads as a gradient rather than as foil.

name: New Wave design
definition: The postmodern break from Swiss order: stair-stepped rules, diagonal and letter-spaced type, weights mixed inside a word, and text reversed out of bars.
useWhen: the Swiss grid kept but deliberately violated

sources.title: Hue and Eye: New Wave graphic design explained
Wikipedia: Wolfgang Weingart

notes: The missing middle between swiss-style and memphis-design: same tools, opposite intent. Weingart taught at Basel, which is why it is called Swiss punk.

name: Frutiger Metro
definition: The flat vector cousin of Frutiger Aero: gradient color blocks, bloom and glow, silhouetted figures, swooshes and abstract flourishes, without the glossy water and grass.
useWhen: gradient vector blocks with bloom and swooshes

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Vectordelia
2000 Aesthetics Wiki: Frutiger Metro

notes: Vectordelia is the wiki name and Frutiger Metro the popular one; both cover the mid 2000s to early 2010s vector poster look, not Microsoft Metro.

name: Constructivism
definition: A 1920s poster language of diagonal bars and blocks, red and black on off-white, photomontage, and heavy sans capitals set on a strong angle.
useWhen: diagonal red and black bars driving the composition

sources.title: daisyUI trends: UI design styles catalog
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Reaches interfaces through hero sections and posters rather than controls; the diagonal is what separates it from De Stijl and Bauhaus.

name: Dot grid background
definition: A faint repeating field of dots or ruled squares behind content, borrowed from graph paper and canvas tools to suggest an editable surface rather than a page.
useWhen: a faint grid or dot field behind the content

sources.title: Magic UI: Dot Pattern
Magic UI: Grid Pattern

notes: Usually one repeating gradient or an SVG tile, masked with a radial fade so it does not compete with the text; the interactive versions light cells under the pointer.
